narrative:
FY2026 budget revenue is GBP 1,833.3M, +1.6% on FY2025 continuing actuals of GBP 1,803.8M. The Q3 forecast stands at GBP 1,812.9M — GBP 20.4M below budget, mainly volume: Regulated Services handbacks came forward and council contact volumes are drifting to digital and the virtual agent.

Central Government remains the largest division at GBP 535.6M (29% of group). Pension Solutions is the fastest-growing (+10.5%) on backlog casework and new scheme work. Regulated Services falls 32.5% as the managed exit runs.

Key risk: per-transaction contact contracts lose revenue as containment rises — the plan must release roster hours at the same pace.

signals.title: Continuing revenue up 1.6% to £906.4m in H1
signals.excerpt: Public Service +2.4% and Pension Solutions +24.7% offset the planned Regulated Services exit; adjusted operating margin 3.6% (H1 2025: 5.3%).

signals.title: £24.4bn pipeline, £998m H1 TCV
signals.excerpt: Book-to-bill 1.1x; Synergy Business Process Services from summer 2027 and a £425m TfL renewal signed in July.

signals.title: Virtual-agent adoption plan — month 3 of 5
signals.source: Capita Contact Centre workforce planning (SDP model)
signals.excerpt: Containment at 18% across about 1,200 customer intents on the 2,000-FTE, 29-contract estate; fall-back-to-human rate 31% on DWP intents.
